titleStmt.title: Paper Prepared in the Department of State

head.hi: Paper Prepared in the Department of State

p.hi: Bringing the Soviets to Closure on START/INF: Four Strategies

div.p: I. Seek to separate START and INF from other subjects, arguing that agreements in these areas are in our mutual interest and should be brought into force.

quote.p: While this is the most straightforward path to realization of START and INF agreements, we cannot assume the Soviets will agree to these reductions without something on defense; they certainly are not prepared to do this now. This leads to consideration of other packages.

div.p: II. Add a ten-year ABM Treaty non-withdrawal commitment, coupling such a commitment to 50% START and 0/100 INF reductions. Negotiations would continue on further steps, including elimination of offensive ballistic missiles.

quote.p: Reduction of strategic forces by 50% and SS–20’s by 90% would be dramatic steps, and would warrant something on defense. If the package permitted some flexibility for testing during this period, a 10-year non-withdrawal commitment would not damage the SDI program, and such an agreement would broaden support for SDI in the Congress.

div.p: III. Execute the START and INF reductions over ten years; and link non-withdrawal to faithful implementation of these reductions.

quote.p: The reductions to 6,000 strategic warheads and 100 INF warheads would be divided into 10 equal increments from 1987 through 1996. We would agree not to withdraw from the ABM Treaty so long as these reductions were faithfully implemented. This would be similar to the first phase of our July 25 proposal, with the reductions deepened from 30% to 50%, and the time stretched from 5–7 years to 10 years. Other aspects, such as elimination of ballistic missiles and sharing the benefits of SDI would be addressed in subsequent negotiations.

div.p: IV. Agree to reduce from 6000 warheads in the second five years to a small residual force.

quote.p:
We can consider such an approach if it becomes necessary to break the current impasse over the reductions in the second five years (elimi
nation of ballistic missiles vs. elimination of strategic forces) in order to secure Soviet agreement to the entire package discussed in Reykjavik.

note.p: Secret; Sensitive. No drafting information appears on the paper.
This proposal is scheduled for publication in Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, vol. V, Soviet Union, March 1985–October 1986.
